Published online:
September 1, 2026 (article dated Sept 1, referencing events through 2026)

Geographic focus:
Global (US, Europe, El Salvador); primary regulatory/market focus on US and EU

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical report [YES] — references Oct 2025 initial announcement, Tether's dominance, SocGen's prior launch
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — Qivalis euro stablecoin launch targeted "later this year"
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — Goldman/BofA/Citi dollar stablecoin targeted H1 2027; ECB monetary policy risks; broader bank-issued stablecoin adoption

Synopsis:
A 21-bank consortium including Goldman Sachs, Bank of America, Citi, and Deutsche Bank is formalizing a company in 2026 to issue a dollar-pegged stablecoin in H1 2027, with euro expansion planned thereafter. They compete with Qivalis (37 institutions, euro stablecoin). The effort rides Trump-era crypto tailwinds but faces a critical headwind: negligible demonstrated demand for bank-issued stablecoins — SocGen's equivalent has only $12.5M in circulation. Tether dominates with $180B+. ECB's Lagarde has flagged systemic risks from private stablecoins.
